title: Pre-Algebra Readiness Gateway
purpose: Determine whether a learner is ready to enter Official Unit 1 or should receive the conditional six-week Unit 0 Foundations & Readiness refresher.

strand_policy.note: With five items per strand, four correct answers equals the 80% strand-readiness threshold. A single result remains a screening signal and should be interpreted alongside course evidence when teacher review is appropriate.

routing.advance: Overall score is at least 80% and every essential strand is at least 80%.
routing.advance_with_targeted_refresh: Overall score is at least 80%, every essential strand is at least 80%, but one or more nonessential strands are below 80%. Learner enters Official Unit 1 with optional targeted refresh recommendations.
routing.unit_0_refresher: Overall score is below 80% OR any essential strand is below 80%. Learner enters Unit 0 Foundations & Readiness.
routing.teacher_review: Use when the attempt is incomplete/invalid, accessibility circumstances materially affect interpretation, or repeated evidence conflicts strongly with the diagnostic result.
routing.unit_0_exit: After Unit 0, learner must demonstrate at least 80% mastery and complete required reasoning corrections before routing directly to Official Unit 1.

naib_record.preservation_rule: This readiness result must never erase or downgrade a prior course-mastery, retention, or completion record.

strands.label: Number Foundations
strands.description: Order of operations, factors/primes, integers, absolute value, and exponent foundations.

strands.label: Rational & Proportional Reasoning
strands.description: Fractions, decimals, percent, ratios, rates, and equivalent representations.

strands.label: Algebraic Reasoning
strands.description: Expressions, substitution, inverse operations, equations, and inequalities.

strands.label: Functions & Coordinates
strands.description: Ordered pairs, coordinate planes, input-output rules, and rate-of-change foundations.

strands.label: Geometry & Measurement
strands.description: Area, perimeter, scale, units, and measurement reasoning.

strands.label: Data & Probability
strands.description: Measures of center, simple probability, data summaries, and representative-sample reasoning.

questions.prompt: Evaluate: 18 - 3 × 4
Which number is a factor of 36?
Which number is prime?
questions.explanation: 31 has exactly two positive factors: 1 and 31.

questions.prompt: Evaluate: -8 + 13
questions.explanation: Moving 13 units right from -8 lands at 5.

questions.prompt: Evaluate: 2³ + |-4|
Evaluate: 3/4 + 1/8
Evaluate: 2.4 ÷ 0.6
What is 15% of 80?
A recipe uses 3 cups of rice for 5 people. At the same rate, how many cups are needed for 20 people?
Which decimal is equivalent to 3/5?
Simplify: 4x + 3x
questions.explanation: The terms are alike, so add the coefficients: 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.prompt: Solve: x + 9 = 23
Solve: 5x = 35
Evaluate 2a + 3 when a = 4.
Solve: x - 2 > 5
In which quadrant is the point (-3, 4)?
questions.explanation: A negative x-coordinate and positive y-coordinate place the point in Quadrant II.

questions.prompt: For y = 2x + 1, what is y when x = 4?
A table has x-values 0, 1, 2 and y-values 3, 5, 7. Which rule fits the table?
questions.explanation: When x increases by 1, y increases by 2, and y = 3 when x = 0, so y = 2x + 3.

questions.prompt: A student records distance traveled after different numbers of hours at a constant speed. Which quantity is the natural input (independent variable)?
questions.explanation: Time is the input used to determine the corresponding distance.

questions.prompt: For every increase of 1 in x, y increases by 3. What is the rate of change?
questions.explanation: Rate of change is change in y divided by change in x: 3 ÷ 1 = 3.

questions.prompt: A triangle has base 10 units and height 6 units. What is its area?
A rectangle is 8 metres long and 5 metres wide. What is its area?
A rectangle is 7 units long and 4 units wide. What is its perimeter?
How many centimetres are in 2.5 metres?
On a scale drawing, 1 cm represents 4 m. A wall measures 6 cm on the drawing. What is the actual length?
What is the mean of 4, 7, 9, and 10?
What is the median of 3, 5, 8, 12, and 20?
questions.explanation: The middle value in the ordered list is 8.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 3 red marbles and 5 blue marbles. What is the probability of drawing a red marble at random?
questions.explanation: There are 3 favorable outcomes among 8 total outcomes, so the probability is 3/8.

questions.prompt: What is the mode of 2, 4, 4, 5, and 7?
questions.explanation: 4 occurs more often than any other value.

questions.prompt: A school wants to know which lunch choices all students prefer. Which sample is most likely to be biased?
options: A random sample from the full student roster
Students selected proportionally from each grade
Only members of the basketball team
A random sample from each lunch period
questions.explanation: Only surveying one team may not represent the preferences of the full school population.
